[h1][b]🎮 Reseña de Stay! Stay! Democratic People's Republic of Korea![/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Si alguna vez pensaste: “Ojalá existiera una novela visual estilo anime, con humor negro, coqueteo incómodo y un tour ‘turístico’ por la República Popular Democrática de Corea… pero con terror psicológico y desnudos”, felicidades: tu algoritmo de Steam te conoce demasiado. Stay! Stay! Democratic People's Republic of Korea! es una aventura indie con ADN de rol ligero (más de decisiones y rutas que de números), que se apoya en la parodia y el shock para mantenerte leyendo.

La propuesta es básicamente: narrativa + elecciones + “simulador de citas” con un trasfondo deliberadamente controversial. La primera impresión es clara: esto no quiere caerle bien a todo el mundo; quiere que lo mires raro, te rías culpablemente y luego te preguntes “¿por qué estoy aquí?”. Y lo más gracioso (o triste): al momento de esta reseña hay 0 jugadores… o sea, estás a punto de entrar a una fiesta donde tú eres la música.

[h2]Lo Glorioso del Régimen y lo Sospechosamente Mejorable[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
✅ Humor sarcástico y paródico con vibra de meme constante 🤡  
✅ Mezcla atrevida de novela visual + citas + terror psicológico 😵‍💫  
✅ “Buena trama” para quienes disfrutan historias incómodas y retorcidas 📖  
✅ Incluye subtítulos, ideal para no perderte el chiste (o el trauma) 📝  
✅ Cromos de Steam: al menos algo coleccionable sale de aquí 🃏  

Lo No Tan Bueno:
❌ 0 jugadores actuales: el multiverso te dejó en visto 👻  
❌ Sin logros: Steam te mira y dice “¿y tu dopamina, campeón?” 🏆🚫  
❌ El combo desnudos/sexual + gore/terror puede sentirse más provocación que sustancia 🔞🩸  
❌ El “rol” se siente más como rutas/decisiones que como sistemas profundos 🎲  
❌ Su controversia puede envejecer raro: hoy te ríes, mañana lo explicas en terapia 🛋️

Stay! Stay! Democratic People's Republic of Korea! es ese juego que algunos van a llamar “valiente sátira” y otros “¿quién aprobó esto?”. Como aventura indie narrativa con toques de rol (por decisiones) cumple: tiene momentos de comedia oscura, tensión psicológica y una intención clara de incomodar. Y sí, a ratos lo logra demasiado bien.

Pero se siente como un producto que vive de su premisa controversial: si conectas con ese humor y ese tono, te lo pasas bien; si no, es probable que lo abandones rápido con la misma energía con la que ignoras términos y condiciones. [h1]Stay! Stay! Democratic People's Republic of Korea![/h1]
Hey you!
Are you longing for an anime dating sim, but hate how most dating sims have trash tier waifus? Are you seeking a game that will make you laugh out loud? Do you want to learn more about the best country ever? no, not Japan you filthy weeaboo! I mean the Democratic People's Republic of Korea! The most majestic and glorious country to ever exist!!!!!
Well then, if the answer to any of these questions is yes. Stay! Stay! Democratic People's Republic of Korea! might be the visual novel for you!!!

[b]Pros[/b]
+ Choose from 2 North Korean beauties to romance (Eunji is best girl).
+ Learn about the culture, history and various locations of the greatest country in existence, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea!
+ Loads of humour! Whether you are familiar with North Korea and the Glorious Leader Kim Jong-un or not, there are laughs to be had (obviously, if you ARE familiar with these things, it makes the game that much more hilarious). 
+ An entertaining story with laughs to be had and, surprisingly, quite a few heartfelt moments and multiple endings too (4, to be precise).
+ The artwork is great, the character sprites and CGs are cute and appealing and are overall very nice to look at (the background images are also of note, as they are quite pleasant and show the surprising beauty of the One True Korea).
+ The intro song is super kawaii, and the BGM is delightful to listen to as well.

[b]Cons[/b]
- Unfortunately, you never get to meet the Glorious Leader Kim Jong-un, and as such, he is not a romance option.
- You are forced to play as a filthy American.
- There is no voice acting (although this could be a good thing depending on your preferences).
- Although there is certainly lewd artwork, for those who enjoy nudity in their dating sims, there is, unfortunately, none to be found on the Steam version of the game... Thankfully, seems the developers have released a free 18+ patch on their website, for those who want to see nude North Korean anime women.

While obviously, I have joked around quite a bit in this review, Stay! Stay! Democratic People's Republic of Korea! is honestly an entertaining visual novel, and I enjoyed it quite a lot, and I can easily recommend it if you want a dating sim that has heartfelt moments, a good sense of humour and tons of references to North Korea.

If travelling to North Korea is not an option for you (not recommended) then maybe this silly parody can at least provide you a general idea. Don't judge book by its cover applies here as it is more than just silly story (won't spoil anything though).

After some epistolary exchange with pen pals from NK you end up on a plane heading there. First important realisation occurs when you realise your pen pals are actually two sisters, on top of being military members, who will also serve as your guide during your stay. Since this is also partly a dating sim you can develop a deeper relationship with them. You are offered several choices which can lead you to one of 4 endings. So there is some replayability which extend the fun quite a bit. The choices offered are mostly straightforward so achieving most endings should be easy. 
Except for quick save/load you have standard gamut of VN's options. Functional and simple.

The anime art from Kopianget is one of the selling points behind this VN. All CGs, backgrounds and character sprites are of above average quality and all fairly detailed but there ain't many of them. Also, there are no animations or cut scenes which is kinda expected of low budget titles like this. There are some vanilla ecchi scenes here which allow me to classify this as an eroge but barely so don't expect much. Overall visual aspects are cutesy and of decent quality.

Audio side here is pretty decent as well. The few tracks present are somewhat above average and fit the events but is nothing is really memorable. The opening/ending song, on the other hand, is rather catchy and very kawaii. Can honestly say that it was an unexpected but pleasant surprise.

No bugs encountered.

To summarise, what have we hare is fairly decent ~6h parody story set in NK with some choices leading to one of the 4 endings. Also, decent art and music. It is honestly better than I expected, especially at this price point. Happy to recommend: 6.7/10

It's got a silly concept and I'm OK with most of it, except there are some major factual errors. No, I'm not talking about exaggerated or satirised or other unrealistic aspects of the story and the setting. After all, the game is about comedy and DPRK is not the easiest country to do research so I can ignore most minor defects but two things are just way, way too off.

The game largely revolves around visiting different landmarks in DPRK and that is one thing you gotta get right. The gate shown in Kaesong is not Kaesong Namdaemun, it's Sungryemun in Seoul. The stadium is not the Yanggakdo Stadium, it is the Rungnado May 1st Stadium (not to be confused with Rungnado PPG, they're on the same islet on the river).

The characters go through Hyesan on their way to Mt. Paektu. The thing is, Hyesan is one of the major points for unauthorised traffic in and out of the country, be it for the smugglers or defectors. If the girls had a plan to defect from the beginning this was the most opportune moment, and far less riskier than sneaking into a cargo ship in Nampo.
